claims.statement: Commission guidance describes flexible connection agreements that limit injections or withdrawals and can offer partial grid access in congested areas. A founder can seek an exclusive site-owner mandate, measured load/generation envelope, and control plan before a DSO application; Polish availability and transferability of such agreements are unverified.

The measurable loss is project delay or cancellation when insufficient grid capacity blocks a renewable, storage, electrification, or charging connection. The Commission cites insufficient capacity, implementation delays, and queue-cleaning reforms; project-specific carrying cost and rejection rates in Poland still need evidence.

The payer hypothesis is a C&I solar, storage, EV-depot, or electrification developer using site-development and interconnection budget at application or acquisition. The Commission estimated very large grid investment needs and warns delays will increase without modernization, but no Polish developer has confirmed a success-fee mandate.

contrary_evidence: Flexible connections can restrict asset output enough to destroy the project economics they are meant to unlock.
DSOs, grid consultants, and EPCs may retain the application relationship, and connection rights may not be assignable or optionable.

economics.acquisition_route: Screen family-business leads and public grid information, model a site-specific flexible operating envelope for five stalled projects, and secure only a conditional owner mandate tied to a DSO-approved connection path before charging a success fee.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A proprietary feeder-level response database and book of qualified site mandates could become a Central European origination platform for storage and flexible loads; material founder equity requires repeat approvals and recurring dispatch revenue after connection.
economics.founder_time: About 12-18 hours per week for modelling and partner coordination; licensed grid engineers and EPCs prepare formal applications.
economics.gross_margin_basis: High-margin analytics and success fees after external engineering; long sales cycles and unsuccessful applications are the primary cost.
economics.payback: Recover screening and engineer-review cost from a small upfront diligence fee, with upside paid only at an accepted connection offer or project sale.
economics.pricing: Fixed connection-options memo, milestone fee at DSO offer, and optional success fee on project financing or sale; later monthly scheduling fee for non-firm operation.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Origination is episodic, but connected flexible assets require recurring scheduling and each DSO outcome improves future site screening.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Feeder-level application outcomes, feasible operating envelopes, and exclusive site-owner mandates
fingerprint.customer: Developers and site owners planning C&I renewables, batteries, EV depots, heat pumps, or other large electric loads
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Renewable installers, landowners, charger EPCs, and grid engineers refer stalled or capacity-constrained sites
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Option-backed flexible-connection origination earning diligence, milestone, success, and later scheduling fees
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Developer pays at connection diligence and again when a usable DSO offer or financeable project is secured
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A viable site cannot obtain the firm grid capacity assumed in its original project design

founder_fit: The family renewable business can surface real stalled projects and installer referrals.
Load-shape modelling, scenario analysis, and site ranking suit the founder's analytical profile.
The wedge buys information and conditional mandates rather than land or grid infrastructure.
risks: Polish DSOs may not offer the relevant flexible agreement or may change rules unpredictably.
A mistaken operating-envelope model can make a project unfinanceable after fees are spent.
Brokerage, engineering, or energy-market activity may require qualifications and careful contract boundaries.

structure.commercial_archetype: Option-backed grid-capacity origination and recurring constrained-operation service
structure.control_point: Exclusive site mandate bound to measured operating data, DSO correspondence, and a feasible flexible envelope
structure.critical_dependency: A DSO-approved non-firm connection whose curtailment terms preserve project economics

thesis: Backcast from grid capacity becoming a time-shaped contractual right rather than a binary connection: win the constrained site's mandate now, redesign it around a flexible envelope, and compound feeder-level acceptance data into an origination advantage.
title: Flexible-Connection Option Desk
uncertainties: Current Polish DSO products, queue rules, and the legal status of conditional site mandates need direct verification.
The share of stalled projects salvageable by flexibility rather than reinforcement is unknown.
No developer has confirmed willingness to pay both diligence and success fees for this intermediary.
